content.content:
700	
701	    drafting:
702	        Drafting stories shows its work in one place, the side panel, docked
703	        at the board's right, as the layout places it, replacing whatever it
704	        held, never in a popup that hides the list. It has
705	        the request box at its top, labelled "Describe what you want", and
706	        beneath it, while the run goes, its research: a muted line of what
707	        the harness is doing, as "Reading the spec…", with its spinner,
708	        updating as it goes, and a "Stop" button. Once it ends, the panel
709	        lists its proposals, as below, then "Accept all" and "Reject all"
710	        buttons along the panel's foot, and closes itself once none is left
711	        to decide. A run that fails shows its error, as the states say, and
712	        leaves the request in its box to try again; one that proposes nothing
713	        says so, as an empty state. Proposals are kept until each is decided,
714	        so closing Planning and coming back finds them as they were.
715	
716	        Drafting can also be started from an open story, with "Ask agent"
717	        in its card's menu or the open story's footer: the request box then
718	        reads "What does this story need?", the run is told the story's
719	        title and prompt, and the drafting panel takes the open story's place
720	        in the side panel, the story's card staying highlighted while the
721	        draft is about it.
722	
723	        A draft about a story, from "Ask agent" or "Draft with agent", may
724	        propose rewriting it: a proposal whose target is the story itself,
725	        to be rewritten, its title, prompt, mode, and spec citations
726	        replaced by the proposal's, its steps and attachments kept; as well
727	        as additions to it, each a step, as the proposals say. Where a
728	        story holds more than one piece of work, the draft splits it: the
729	        story's rewrite comes first, the first piece, with its steps, and
730	        each other piece is a proposal for a new story of its own, its
731	        target "New story", with its own title, prompt, mode, and spec
732	        citations, grounded as the spec grounding says. A story that is one
733	        piece of work gets only its rewrite and its steps, and no new story.
734	
735	        A draft favours several stories over one story of many steps. Each
736	        story it proposes is one piece of work a single chain does: as a
737	        rule a Chain story, its prompt changing the spec and then the code to
738	        match it, with at most one step, a Spec step following the chain up,
739	        where the spec needs settling once the code is done. Work that would
740	        need more than that is split into stories of their own, each a "New
741	        story" proposal, never strung onto one story as further steps.
742	        Another mode, Code, Spec, Ask, or Freeform, is proposed only for a
743	        story that is only that, as a question or a change to the code
744	        alone. A story drafted that already has steps keeps them, as a
745	        rewrite keeps them; the draft proposes no more beyond the one Spec
746	        follow-up, and proposes as new stories what further steps would
747	        have done.
748	
749	        The request is sent with the panel's "Draft" button, its primary
750	        action, or by pressing Enter in the request box, whichever label it
751	        reads; Ctrl+Enter there starts it too, and the button's tooltip
752	        gives Enter as its shortcut. Shift+Enter adds a new line in the box
753	        and sends nothing. A request that is empty, or only spaces and new
754	        lines, starts nothing, and the button is disabled while it is. While
755	        a run is going, Enter starts no second one, and the button is
756	        disabled. Enter in the request box only ever sends the request: the
757	        list's Enter, opening or closing the focused story, never fires
758	        while focus is in the box.
759	
760	    draftingWithAgent:
761	        Several stories can be drafted at once, each in a run of its own.
762	        "Draft with agent" is an item of the menu of every card in Draft,
763	        the Backlog, and Next sprint, the menu its hover button opens and
764	        right-clicking opens at the pointer, as the parts say, and a button
765	        of the bulk bar, drafting every selected story; a card in Current
766	        sprint or Done, and a finding, has no such item. It is meant mainly
767	        for Draft's rough stories, but drafts any story it is offered on.
768	
769	        Each story drafts as "Ask agent" drafts an open story, with no
770	        request box and nothing to type: the run is told the story's title,
771	        its prompt, its mode, and its steps, and asked to turn it into a
772	        full story, a fuller prompt, the mode that fits it, its Spec
773	        follow-up step where it needs one, and its spec citations, shaped
774	        as drafting says, grounded as the spec grounding says;
775	        and, where the story holds more than one piece of work, to split
776	        it, as drafting says: the story's rewrite, the first piece, with its
777	        steps, then a "New story" proposal for each other piece, each with
778	        its own title, prompt, mode, and spec citations, grounded the same
779	        way. A story that is one piece of work gets only its rewrite and its
780	        steps.
781	        Each run is its own, in a run of its own with no session, a Question
782	        run as the proposals say, with the planning prompt of the
783	        @{BakedSystemPrompts}. All the runs start at once, none waiting on
784	        another, however many stories are drafted; one ending, failing, or
785	        being stopped never touches the others. A story already drafting is
786	        skipped, so drafting it again starts no second run.
787	
788	        The drafts never take over the side panel, which holds only one
789	        thing at a time, as the layout says: a story drafting this way
790	        shows its run on its own card, and opening the story while it
791	        drafts shows the story in the panel as ever, its run going on. While
792	        its run goes, the card's property row shows the loading state, as
793	        the states say, "Drafting…" with its spinner, in place of its
794	        status, and its menu has "Stop", which stops that run alone and
795	        keeps whatever it had proposed by then, in place of "Draft with
796	        agent". A run that fails shows its error on that card, beneath its
797	        property row, as the states say, in the theme's error colour with
798	        "Details" collapsed and "Try again", which drafts the story again;
799	        the error stays until the story is drafted again or opened. A run
800	        cut off when the application quits, as every run is, shows the same
801	        error once it is open again.
802	
803	        When a run ends, its card's property row shows how many of its
804	        proposals are waiting, as "3 proposals", in the theme's accent, or
805	        "1 proposal", counting down as each is decided and gone once none
806	        is left, counting every kind: its rewrite, its additions, and its
807	        new stories; a run that proposed nothing shows "Nothing proposed",
808	        muted, until the story is next opened. Opening the story shows them
809	        all in the side panel, beneath the story's own fields, under a
810	        "Proposals" heading, as proposal cards, as the proposal cards say,
811	        each new story's card labelled "New story", in the order the run
812	        gave them, its rewrite first, then its new stories and additions in
813	        the order given, with "Accept all" and "Reject all" beneath the
814	        last; "Accept all" accepts the rewrite, every addition, and every
815	        new story together. Drafting a
816	        story again while proposals of its wait adds the new ones after
817	        them.
818	
819	        A story's waiting proposals are kept until each is decided, saved
820	        with the plan as soon as its run ends, in
821	        `.suspense/planning/proposals/`, a file per story named by its id,
822	        so they come back, and its card's count with them, after closing
823	        Planning, a reload, or a restart. A story deleted takes its waiting
824	        proposals with it, and one duplicated copies none.
825	
826	        Nothing reaches the plan until it is accepted, as the proposals
827	        say. Accepting the story's rewrite rewrites it as proposed, and
828	        accepting an addition adds its step to the story's end, as the
829	        proposal cards say. Accepting a new story split off it adds that
830	        story at the end of the Backlog, marked "From agent", as the
831	        proposal cards say, never into Draft and never into Next sprint. A
832	        story in Draft whose rewrite or addition is accepted moves to the
833	        end of the Backlog, as "Move to backlog" moves it and motion
834	        animates it, staying open if it was; accepting a new story split off
835	        it never moves it, and a story in the Backlog or Next sprint stays
836	        where it is. A story sent while
837	        its proposals waited can no longer be rewritten or added to, as the
838	        proposal cards say.
839	
840	    proposals:
841	        The agent never writes the plan itself. Its run is a Question run,
842	        as the @{Sandbox} says, able to read the project and change nothing,
843	        and Suspense data is never granted to it, so it can't touch
844	        `.suspense/planning/`; it only proposes, and nothing it proposes
845	        reaches the plan until the user accepts it.
846	
847	        Each proposal is one concrete task, with a title, a prompt, and the
848	        mode that fits it, and says where it should go: either "New story",
849	        to become a story of its own, or "Add to" a story, naming an existing
850	        story the run was shown, the open story first, to be added to it,
851	        or, in a draft about a story, "Rewrite", the story itself rewritten,
852	        as drafting says. The
853	        planning prompt of the @{BakedSystemPrompts} asks for each proposal
854	        as a fenced block whose info string is `suspense-story`, holding its
855	        title, its mode, its target, `new`, the story's id, or `rewrite`, its `spec`
856	        list of citations into the Piton source, as the spec grounding says,
857	        and its prompt, so the application reads it whatever else the reply
858	        says. The planning prompt explains the form with an example, as:
859	
860	        \\\
861	        ```suspense-story
862	        title: Close a finished sprint
863	        mode: chain
864	        target: new
865	        spec:
866	        - spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.sprint: when Close sprint shows
867	        - No match: archiving a closed sprint
868	        prompt:
869	        Close sprint is offered once every story of the current sprint has
870	        ended, as spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.sprint says.
871	        ```
872	        \\\
873	
874	        A
875	        block that names a story that no longer exists is shown as "New
876	        story", with a muted note saying so.
877	
878	    specGrounding:
879	        A drafted story is grounded in the project's spec, never written
880	        from the request alone. Before proposing, the drafter searches the
881	        spec for what each story touches: the requirements and behaviours it
882	        changes or relies on, the names it uses, as a feature, a component,
883	        or a property, and the sections they are in. It reads the spec as
884	        every run does, from its compiled reference or from what `piton
885	        slice` prints, never from the Piton source, as the
886	        @{ModeSystemPrompts} says, and the planning prompt of the
887	        @{BakedSystemPrompts} tells it to.
888	
889	        Each proposal cites what it found, specifically: its `suspense-story`
890	        block holds a `spec` list, one entry per element, each a link to the
891	        element in the spec's Piton source, under the spec location, never
892	        to the compiled reference: the .pi file, relative to the project
893	        directory, then `#` and the element it names, an anchor or a
894	        property on one, in the form `piton slice` takes, as
895	        `spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.sprint`, with a short line of
896	        what in it the story touches. The story's prompt names those
897	        elements and links to them in the same form. Only elements the
898	        drafter found are cited, and where they point is the only thing
899	        that is Piton source: the drafter still learns what the spec says
900	        only from the compiled reference or from what `piton slice` prints,
901	        never by reading the Piton source, as the @{ModeSystemPrompts} says,
902	        and works out each element's source from what `piton slice` prints
903	        for it, which names the file each declaration is in.
904	
905	        The application checks each link against the Piton source when the
906	        proposal arrives: the file has to exist under the spec location, and
907	        has to define the named element, the anchor declared in it and, for
908	        a property, that property on it, as `piton slice` would find it. A
909	        link that fails either check is dropped, with a muted note on the
910	        card saying which link it dropped and why, "no such file" or "the
911	        file doesn't define Planning.sprint". Each citation, on the proposal
912	        card and in an accepted story's "Spec" list, opens that place in the
913	        Piton source, the file in the editor at the element's declaration,
914	        as the @{OpenFile} opens a file.
915	
916	        Where no spec element matches part of a story, as a request for

drafting:
        Drafting stories shows its work in one place, the side panel, docked
        at the board's right, as the layout places it, replacing whatever it
        held, never in a popup that hides the list. It has
        the request box at its top, labelled "Describe what you want", and
        beneath it, while the run goes, its research: a muted line of what
        the harness is doing, as "Reading the spec…", with its spinner,
        updating as it goes, and a "Stop" button. Once it ends, the panel
        lists its proposals, as below, then "Accept all" and "Reject all"
        buttons along the panel's foot, and closes itself once none is left
        to decide. A run that fails shows its error, as the states say, and
        leaves the request in its box to try again; one that proposes nothing
        says so, as an empty state. Proposals are kept until each is decided,
        so closing Planning and coming back finds them as they were.

        Drafting can also be started from an open story, with "Ask agent"
        in its card's menu or the open story's footer: the request box then
        reads "What does this story need?", the run is told the story's
        title and prompt, and the drafting panel takes the open story's place
        in the side panel, the story's card staying highlighted while the
        draft is about it.

        A draft about a story, from "Ask agent" or "Draft with agent", may
        propose rewriting it: a proposal whose target is the story itself,
        to be rewritten, its title, prompt, mode, and spec citations
        replaced by the proposal's, its steps and attachments kept; as well
        as additions to it, each a step, as the proposals say. Where a
        story holds more than one piece of work, the draft splits it: the
        story's rewrite comes first, the first piece, with its steps, and
        each other piece is a proposal for a new story of its own, its
        target "New story", with its own title, prompt, mode, and spec
        citations, grounded as the spec grounding says. A story that is one
        piece of work gets only its rewrite and its steps, and no new story.

        A draft favours several stories over one story of many steps. Each
        story it proposes is one piece of work a single chain does: as a
        rule a Chain story, its prompt changing the spec and then the code to
        match it, with at most one step, a Spec step following the chain up,
        where the spec needs settling once the code is done. Work that would
        need more than that is split into stories of their own, each a "New
        story" proposal, never strung onto one story as further steps.
        Another mode, Code, Spec, Ask, or Freeform, is proposed only for a
        story that is only that, as a question or a change to the code
        alone. A story drafted that already has steps keeps them, as a
        rewrite keeps them; the draft proposes no more beyond the one Spec
        follow-up, and proposes as new stories what further steps would
        have done.

        The request is sent with the panel's "Draft" button, its primary
        action, or by pressing Enter in the request box, whichever label it
        reads; Ctrl+Enter there starts it too, and the button's tooltip
        gives Enter as its shortcut. Shift+Enter adds a new line in the box
        and sends nothing. A request that is empty, or only spaces and new
        lines, starts nothing, and the button is disabled while it is. While
        a run is going, Enter starts no second one, and the button is
        disabled. Enter in the request box only ever sends the request: the
        list's Enter, opening or closing the focused story, never fires
        while focus is in the box.

    draftingWithAgent:
        Several stories can be drafted at once, each in a run of its own.
        "Draft with agent" is an item of the menu of every card in Draft,
        the Backlog, and Next sprint, the menu its hover button opens and
        right-clicking opens at the pointer, as the parts say, and a button
        of the bulk bar, drafting every selected story; a card in Current
        sprint or Done, and a finding, has no such item. It is meant mainly
        for Draft's rough stories, but drafts any story it is offered on.

        Each story drafts as "Ask agent" drafts an open story, with no
        request box and nothing to type: the run is told the story's title,
        its prompt, its mode, and its steps, and asked to turn it into a
        full story, a fuller prompt, the mode that fits it, its Spec
        follow-up step where it needs one, and its spec citations, shaped
        as drafting says, grounded as the spec grounding says;
        and, where the story holds more than one piece of work, to split
        it, as drafting says: the story's rewrite, the first piece, with its
        steps, then a "New story" proposal for each other piece, each with
        its own title, prompt, mode, and spec citations, grounded the same
        way. A story that is one piece of work gets only its rewrite and its
        steps.
        Each run is its own, in a run of its own with no session, a Question
        run as the proposals say, with the planning prompt of the
        @{BakedSystemPrompts}. All the runs start at once, none waiting on
        another, however many stories are drafted; one ending, failing, or
        being stopped never touches the others. A story already drafting is
        skipped, so drafting it again starts no second run.

        The drafts never take over the side panel, which holds only one
        thing at a time, as the layout says: a story drafting this way
        shows its run on its own card, and opening the story while it
        drafts shows the story in the panel as ever, its run going on. While
        its run goes, the card's property row shows the loading state, as
        the states say, "Drafting…" with its spinner, in place of its
        status, and its menu has "Stop", which stops that run alone and
        keeps whatever it had proposed by then, in place of "Draft with
        agent". A run that fails shows its error on that card, beneath its
        property row, as the states say, in the theme's error colour with
        "Details" collapsed and "Try again", which drafts the story again;
        the error stays until the story is drafted again or opened. A run
        cut off when the application quits, as every run is, shows the same
        error once it is open again.

        When a run ends, its card's property row shows how many of its
        proposals are waiting, as "3 proposals", in the theme's accent, or
        "1 proposal", counting down as each is decided and gone once none
        is left, counting every kind: its rewrite, its additions, and its
        new stories; a run that proposed nothing shows "Nothing proposed",
        muted, until the story is next opened. Opening the story shows them
        all in the side panel, beneath the story's own fields, under a
        "Proposals" heading, as proposal cards, as the proposal cards say,
        each new story's card labelled "New story", in the order the run
        gave them, its rewrite first, then its new stories and additions in
        the order given, with "Accept all" and "Reject all" beneath the
        last; "Accept all" accepts the rewrite, every addition, and every
        new story together. Drafting a
        story again while proposals of its wait adds the new ones after
        them.

        A story's waiting proposals are kept until each is decided, saved
        with the plan as soon as its run ends, in
        `.suspense/planning/proposals/`, a file per story named by its id,
        so they come back, and its card's count with them, after closing
        Planning, a reload, or a restart. A story deleted takes its waiting
        proposals with it, and one duplicated copies none.

        Nothing reaches the plan until it is accepted, as the proposals
        say. Accepting the story's rewrite rewrites it as proposed, and
        accepting an addition adds its step to the story's end, as the
        proposal cards say. Accepting a new story split off it adds that
        story at the end of the Backlog, marked "From agent", as the
        proposal cards say, never into Draft and never into Next sprint. A
        story in Draft whose rewrite or addition is accepted moves to the
        end of the Backlog, as "Move to backlog" moves it and motion
        animates it, staying open if it was; accepting a new story split off
        it never moves it, and a story in the Backlog or Next sprint stays
        where it is. A story sent while
        its proposals waited can no longer be rewritten or added to, as the
        proposal cards say.

    proposals:
        The agent never writes the plan itself. Its run is a Question run,
        as the @{Sandbox} says, able to read the project and change nothing,
        and Suspense data is never granted to it, so it can't touch
        `.suspense/planning/`; it only proposes, and nothing it proposes
        reaches the plan until the user accepts it.

        Each proposal is one concrete task, with a title, a prompt, and the
        mode that fits it, and says where it should go: either "New story",
        to become a story of its own, or "Add to" a story, naming an existing
        story the run was shown, the open story first, to be added to it,
        or, in a draft about a story, "Rewrite", the story itself rewritten,
        as drafting says. The
        planning prompt of the @{BakedSystemPrompts} asks for each proposal
        as a fenced block whose info string is `suspense-story`, holding its
        title, its mode, its target, `new`, the story's id, or `rewrite`, its `spec`
        list of citations into the Piton source, as the spec grounding says,
        and its prompt, so the application reads it whatever else the reply
        says. The planning prompt explains the form with an example, as:

        \\\
        ```suspense-story
        title: Close a finished sprint
        mode: chain
        target: new
        spec:
        - spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.sprint: when Close sprint shows
        - No match: archiving a closed sprint
        prompt:
        Close sprint is offered once every story of the current sprint has
        ended, as spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.sprint says.
        ```
        \\\

        A
        block that names a story that no longer exists is shown as "New
        story", with a muted note saying so.

    specGrounding:
        A drafted story is grounded in the project's spec, never written
        from the request alone. Before proposing, the drafter searches the
        spec for what each story touches: the requirements and behaviours it
        changes or relies on, the names it uses, as a feature, a component,
        or a property, and the sections they are in. It reads the spec as
        every run does, from its compiled reference or from what `piton
        slice` prints, never from the Piton source, as the
        @{ModeSystemPrompts} says, and the planning prompt of the
        @{BakedSystemPrompts} tells it to.

        Each proposal cites what it found, specifically: its `suspense-story`
        block holds a `spec` list, one entry per element, each a link to the
        element in the spec's Piton source, under the spec location, never
        to the compiled reference: the .pi file, relative to the project
        directory, then `#` and the element it names, an anchor or a
        property on one, in the form `piton slice` takes, as
        `spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.sprint`, with a short line of
        what in it the story touches. The story's prompt names those
        elements and links to them in the same form. Only elements the
        drafter found are cited, and where they point is the only thing
        that is Piton source: the drafter still learns what the spec says
        only from the compiled reference or from what `piton slice` prints,
        never by reading the Piton source, as the @{ModeSystemPrompts} says,
        and works out each element's source from what `piton slice` prints
        for it, which names the file each declaration is in.

        The application checks each link against the Piton source when the
        proposal arrives: the file has to exist under the spec location, and
        has to define the named element, the anchor declared in it and, for
        a property, that property on it, as `piton slice` would find it. A
        link that fails either check is dropped, with a muted note on the
        card saying which link it dropped and why, "no such file" or "the
        file doesn't define Planning.sprint". Each citation, on the proposal
        card and in an accepted story's "Spec" list, opens that place in the
        Piton source, the file in the editor at the element's declaration,
        as the @{OpenFile} opens a file.

        Where no spec element matches part of a story, as a request for
        something the spec doesn't describe yet, the story says so instead
        of inventing one: its `spec` list holds an entry reading "No match",
        with what was looked for, and its prompt says plainly that the spec
        has nothing on it yet, so the change is new. A proposal with no
        element at all, and no "No match", isn't shown as a story: its card
        says the drafter cited no spec, in the theme's warning colour, with
        "Draft again", which runs the draft for that story once more.

        The citations are shown on the proposal's card, beneath its prompt,
        as a short list, each element's name, as `Planning.sprint`, and its
        file, muted, as a link that opens that place in the Piton source, a
        "No match" entry muted with a small marker, and are kept with the
        story once it is accepted, listed in the open story beneath its
        steps as "Spec", and shown in its card's tooltip. They can be edited
        with the story, removed, or added to by hand: "Add citation" opens a
        picker of the spec's elements, its anchors and their properties,
        found from the Piton source and searched by name, never from the
        compiled reference, and adds the one picked in the same form,
        checked as a proposal's are.

        Each citation says what kind of element it is, "Requirement",
        "Behaviour", "Name", or "Section", shown as a small muted label
        before it, and quotes the few words of the spec it rests on, so what
        the story relies on can be checked at a glance. Grounding holds for
        every proposal, however it came: from Draft stories, from research
        that ends with proposals, and from an Ask answer's `suspense-story`
        block, each checked and flagged the same way when it arrives.

    proposalCards:
        Each proposal is a card in the panel, in the order given: a label at
        its top, "New story" in the theme's accent, or, for an addition,
        "Add to this story" where it targets the story the research or draft
        was started from, "Rewrite this story" for a rewrite, and "Add to"
        and the story's title otherwise, in
        the story's own mode's colour, so where it will go is always read
        before anything else on the card; its title,
        its mode pill, and its prompt beneath, clipped at four lines with
        "Read more"; and three buttons along its foot, "Accept", "Edit", and
        "Reject", reachable by Tab and labelled for a screen reader. Edit
        opens the card's title, prompt, mode, and target in place, the target
        a menu of "New story" and each story, to be changed before it is
        accepted; editing doesn't accept it. Reject removes the card, with a
        short "Undo" in its place for a few seconds.

        Accept records it in the plan straight away, saved as any change to
        the plan is: a new story goes into the Backlog, at its end, in its
        mode, marked "From agent" with a small sparkle beside its title until
        it is first opened, its spec citations kept with it, whether it was
        accepted on its own card or with "Accept all", and whether it came
        from drafting, research, or an Ask answer. Accepting never adds
        anything to Next sprint, so it never starts a sprint, however Start
        automatically is set; an accepted story reaches a sprint only once it
        is moved to Next sprint, as the sprint says; an addition is added to the named story as a new
        step at its end, as its steps say, its attachments with it, and the
        story is marked "Updated by agent" until it is next opened, the new
        step shown highlighted the first time it is; where the story no
        longer exists by then, the step isn't added, as the steps say, and
        the card stays, its target changed to "New story", to be accepted
        again; a rewrite replaces the story's title, prompt, mode, and spec
        citations with the proposal's, keeping its steps and attachments,
        and marks it "Updated by agent" the same way, and where the story no
        longer exists by then, it is changed to "New story" the same way. A
        story already sent can't be added to or rewritten: its
        proposals offer only "New story". Each card, once decided, goes from
        the panel, and an accepted one leaves a one-line muted note in its
        place, "Added to Backlog" or "Added to <story>", with a link that
        opens the story where it is, in the Backlog or its section.

        Ask answers can propose the same way: a `suspense-story` block in an
        answer is shown as a proposal card, with the same Accept, Edit, and

        can come out of a conversation without anything written silently.

33:Each proposal is one concrete task, with a title, a prompt, and the mode that fits it, and says where it should go: either "New story", to become a story of its own, or "Add to" a story, naming an existing story the run was shown, to be added to it. A draft about a story, from "Ask agent" or "Draft with agent", proposes only new stories, as drafting says, never one that adds to or rewrites the story drafted. The planning prompt of the [BakedSystemPrompts](../harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts) asks for each proposal as a fenced block whose info string is `suspense-story`, holding its title, its mode, its target, `new` or the story's id, its `spec` list of citations into the Piton source, as the spec grounding says, and its prompt, so the application reads it whatever else the reply says. A new story's Spec follow-up step, in a draft about a story, is a block of its own just after the story it follows, its target `step`, holding the step's mode, Spec, and its prompt, and is read as that story's step, part of its proposal and never a proposal apart. The planning prompt explains the form with an example, as:
37:target: new
45:A block that names a story that no longer exists is shown as "New story", with a muted note saying so. In a draft about a story, a block whose target is the story drafted, by its id or as `rewrite`, as one saved before drafts proposed only new stories, is read as `new`, and its card reads "New story"; a block that would add a step to the story drafted is read as the follow-up step of the new story just before it, or, where there is none, as a new story of its own.
50:Each proposal is a card in the panel, in the order given: a label at its top, "New story" in the theme's accent, or, for an addition, "Add to this story" where it targets the story the research was started from, and "Add to" and the story's title otherwise, in the story's own mode's colour, so where it will go is always read before anything else on the card. On a draft about a story, every card reads "New story", and none reads "Rewrite this story" or "Add to this story". Beneath the label come its title, its mode pill, and its prompt, clipped at four lines with "Read more"; its follow-up step, where it has one, beneath its prompt, as part of the story it follows, step 2 with its mode pill and the first line of its prompt, never a card of its own; and three buttons along its foot, "Accept", "Edit", and "Reject", reachable by Tab and labelled for a screen reader. Edit opens the card's title, prompt, mode, and target in place, the target a menu of "New story" and each story, on a draft about a story every story but the one drafted, to be changed before it is accepted; editing doesn't accept it. Reject removes the card, with a short "Undo" in its place for a few seconds.
51:Accept records it in the plan straight away, saved as any change to the plan is: a new story goes into the Backlog, at its end, in its mode, marked "From agent" with a small sparkle beside its title until it is first opened, its spec citations kept with it, whether it was accepted on its own card or with "Accept all", and whether it came from drafting, research, or an Ask answer. Accepting never adds anything to Next sprint, so it never starts a sprint, however Start automatically is set; an accepted story reaches a sprint only once it is moved to Next sprint, as the sprint says; an addition is added to the named story as a new step at its end, as its steps say, its attachments with it, and the story is marked "Updated by agent" until it is next opened, the new step shown highlighted the first time it is; where the story no longer exists by then, the step isn't added, as the steps say, and the card stays, its target changed to "New story", to be accepted again. A new story from a draft about a story carries its follow-up step as its own step, after its prompt, and accepting it never changes the story drafted, nor moves it, nor marks it "Updated by agent". A story already sent can't be added to: its proposals offer only "New story". Each card, once decided, goes from the panel, and an accepted one leaves a one-line muted note in its place, "Added to Backlog" or "Added to <story>", with a link that opens the story where it is, in the Backlog or its section.

content.text:
I've changed the spec so that accepting a story's draft never touches the drafted story. Every suggestion now becomes a new story at the end of the Backlog, as `Planning.creating` says. `piton check` and `piton build` both pass. I didn't change any code.

What the code should follow in `spec/scope/planning/index.pi`:

- **`Planning.drafting`**: a draft from "Draft with agent" or "Ask agent" never changes the drafted story. What used to be the rewrite comes first as a "New story", with the proposed title, prompt, mode and spec citations. Its Spec follow-up step comes with it as its own step. Every other piece is also a new story. Nothing in such a draft targets the drafted story.
- **`Planning.draftingWithAgent`**:
  - The card's proposal count counts each new story once; its follow-up step isn't counted separately.
  - "Accept all" creates every new story together, at the end of the Backlog, in the order given.
  - Accepting never changes the drafted story, never moves a Draft story to the Backlog, and never marks it "Updated by agent". Proposals on a story that was sent while they waited can still be accepted as new stories.
- **`Planning.proposals`**: the `suspense-story` target is now `new` or a story id; `rewrite` is gone. I had to decide how a draft returns the follow-up step, since the block had no place for it: as a separate block with `target: step` right after the story it follows, read as that story's step. For drafts about a story, the code should also accept old or stray blocks. A block targeting the drafted story (by id or `rewrite`) is read as `new`. A block adding a step to the drafted story becomes the step of the new story just before it, or a new story if there's none before it.
- **`Planning.proposalCards`**:
  - On a draft about a story, every card reads "New story"; none reads "Rewrite this story" or "Add to this story".
  - The follow-up step shows on its story's card as step 2, under the prompt.
  - Edit's target menu leaves out the drafted story.
  - Accepting a new story adds its step and never changes the drafted story.
  - Additions from Ask answers and research work as before.

I left one thing alone because it wasn't in the four sections you named: the planning prompt in `BakedSystemPrompts` (`planning.pi`) still says it proposes a story's "rewrite". It should probably be updated so the agent stops proposing rewrites. I also chose `step` as the target name myself, so you may want to settle that before the code step.
